Bring your dog—or come without one—and help Labs and More give rescued dogs a second chance at the 13th Annual Howl-O-Ween Mutt Run/Walk on Saturday, October 24!

events.title: Wildlife Rescue by the Sea
events.description:
What happens when wildlife needs help—and what happens after an animal is rescued?
Join Wildlife Jewels® for a special community evening at The Naked Cafe exploring Solana Beach’s remarkable wildlife through real rescue stories, wildlife rehabilitation, art, and conversation.
Dr. Azi Sharif, Founder & Executive Director of Wildlife Jewels, will share stories and discoveries from the organization’s coastal monitoring and bird rescue work, including the seabird starvation and mortality event witnessed along our coast this spring. Learn how to recognize signs of wildlife in distress and what to do when an animal may need help.
Special guest Dr. Erica Ellis, Medical Director of Shalom Wildlife Hospital, will take guests behind the scenes of wildlife rehabilitation and share what it takes to give injured and orphaned wildlife a second chance in the wild.
Throughout the evening, art and photography from the Wildlife Jewels® Collections will be showcased throughout The Naked Cafe, celebrating rescued animals and the remarkable wildlife of our coast.
Come discover the wildlife living all around us and learn how each of us can help protect it.

events.title: Spreckels Organ Society presents The Phantom of the Opera in Concert
events.address: 2125 Pan American Rd E, San Diego
events.description:
The Spreckels Organ Society and San Diego Civic Organist Raúl Prieto Ramírez presents thrilling organ solos and a concert version of The Phantom of the Opera with soprano Caroline Nelms and tenor Cole Tornberg, showcasing the Spreckels Organ – the largest open-air musical instrument in the world!
Always free and open to the public – this concert with spooky lights, will also include eerie projections. Guests are also encouraged to come dressed in costume and take a photo on stage with the artists after the concert.
Set in the beautiful backdrop of Balboa Park’s open-air venue, where performances bring a one-of-a-kind experience for guests. The elevated music venue brings world-class artists for San Diegans and visitors to enjoy for free. Parking in Balboa Park is free after 6:00 p.m.
The Spreckels Organ Society is a nonprofit organization that curates concerts and performances at the Spreckels Organ Pavilion, located in the heart of Balboa Park. They also host weekly concerts every Sunday at 2:00 p.m.
Through the generosity of the City of San Diego, the weekly Spreckels Organ Society concerts are presented at no charge in accordance with the 1915 Deed of Gift, whereby the brothers John and Adolph Spreckels gave the Spreckels Organ and Pavilion to the City of San Diego. Donations are always accepted.
For more information about the Spreckels Organ Society, visit www.SpreckelsOrgan.org.

events.title: 26th Annual Fall Back Festival
events.venue: Gaslamp Museum at the Davis-Horton House
events.description:
Get ready to turn back the clock—literally! On Sunday, November 1, 2026, as daylight savings time ends, the Gaslamp Quarter transforms into a vibrant celebration of history at the 26th Annual Fall Back Festival. From 12 p.m. to 4 p.m., the streets surrounding the iconic Davis-Horton House at 4th and Island Avenue will transport visitors to a bygone era, filled with historic fun, hands-on learning, and memorable adventures for the entire family.
Now in its 26th year, Fall Back Festival has become a beloved San Diego tradition—where families gather to experience old-fashioned amusements, cultural demonstrations, and timeless community spirit. As the clocks "fall back," so does the Gaslamp Quarter, offering an immersive afternoon where history truly comes to life.
Bring your loved ones for a Sunday brimming with interactive activities and entertainment: watch in awe as a talented blacksmith forges iron, join the laughter and cheers of a pie-eating contest, feel the rhythm of the Kumeyaay Drum Circle, and explore dozens of engaging attractions designed to spark curiosity and delight children of all ages.
Activities and Demonstrations for this year’s fest include:
- Caricaturist and Face Painter
- Penny Candy Booth
- Fun Competitions for Prizes & Giveaways
- Root Beer Float Bar
- Stagecoach Photo-Op
- Kumeyaay Bird Songs and Dances
- Native California Tools & Weaponry
This FREE event is more than just a festival—it’s a living time capsule, blending San Diego’s rich cultural heritage with a playful family street fair atmosphere. Kids can step into the shoes of early San Diegans, while parents enjoy the nostalgia and energy of an afternoon designed to connect generations.
Fall Back Festival is proudly presented by the Gaslamp Quarter Historical Foundation and plays a vital role in advancing their mission to preserve the history and culture of the Gaslamp Quarter, providing a living history of San Diego for all to enjoy.
For more information, please contact 619-233-4692 or visit Gaslampmuseum.org
